surprises_or_findings: Idempotency-key shape divergence (AC #5 surface point): the existing coherence-escalation rule uses (rule-name, epicId, stage) — three components, no anomalyType. This bead's stuck-in-stage rule uses (rule-name, epicId, stage, anomalyType, windowStart) — five components. Two reasons for the divergence: (a) AC #1 forbids changing existing skip conditions, including the 15-min windowStart bucketing which lets the rule refire after a failed dispatch; (b) ADR-015 § Consequences names anomalyType as a cross-rule de-dup discriminator (refinement of ADR-009). For stuck-in-stage's purposes the anomalyType is a constant ('stuck-in-stage'), so it adds no behavioural change today, but it future-proofs the key against new rules that might detect different anomalyTypes on the same (epicId, stage). Cross-rule de-dup with coherence-escalation continues to work because the rule-name prefix differs (`stuck-in-stage::...` vs `coherence-escalation::...`); the reconciler core's dedup is per (rule-name, key) so both rules can fire independently. — EventSummary import path: imported as `type EventSummary` from '../coherence-journal' per wlsr.2's marker decision (EventSummary = PipelineEvent re-export). No redefinition. — dispatchHistory field source (RISK FLAGS surface point): there is no `dispatchHistory` field on EpicSnapshot or any ReconcilerSnapshot type. Derived at match-time from `reconciler-action-taken` events scoped to the epic, sorted newest-first; entries surface ruleName + idempotencyKey + (when present) context.resumeAction. This matches how repeat-dispatch-escalation reads dispatch history from the same event source (its own context.recentActions field). — marker omission per ADR-015 § 3: stuck-in-stage is event-log-triggered, not marker-triggered, so EscalationContext.marker is left undefined — coherence will read events.jsonl directly during diagnosis, marker is not the triggering signal here. — STAGE_RESUME_ACTIONS used as detection predicate: AC #1 says 'do NOT change skip conditions'; the existing matches() skips stages not in STAGE_RESUME_ACTIONS. AC #3 says 'unused by act()'. Both are satisfied: matches() retains the skip; act() makes no reference. The constant has effectively two roles now: (1) detection-time predicate (matches), (2) advisory data inside ruleSpecificContext.dispatchHistory.resumeAction (read from prior reconciler-action-taken event payloads, not from the constant directly). The retire-after-empirical-verification follow-on bead will need to handle (1) explicitly — e.g., replace the membership check with an explicit stage-allowlist enum.
